Year one hundred.
A hundred years later, the surface is a frozen wasteland.
No sunlight.
No forests.
No normal ecosystems.
Just darkness and ice.
Yet deep beneath the oceans, life could still survive.
Because some organisms don't need sunlight at all.
They live on heat and chemicals from deep inside the Earth.
So even without the Sun, life might continue.
Just not the life we know.
Year one thousand.
Earth would now be a frozen planet, drifting silently through space.
And that is perhaps the most terrifying part.
The Earth wouldn't explode.
Humanity wouldn't disappear instantly.
The planet would simply, slowly, freeze.
Until almost everything we know became a memory.
So if the Sun disappeared tomorrow, how long do you think humanity would actually survive?
